chunks: We were informed by al-Hakim, Abu Hamid, Ahmad bin Hussain bin Ali, in Balkh, that he said: We were told by Abu Abdillah al-Bukhari, that he said: We were told by Sahl bin Mutawakkhil, that he said: We were told by Sulayman bin Abi Shaykh, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hakam, from ‘Uwana, that he said: Ali bin Abi Talib, Allah’s blessings be upon him, said on the Day of Jamal to Aisha: How have you seen the making of Allah to you, O Humaira? She said to him: You have ruled (by winning), so pardon. It means: Be generous.

key_terms.حُمَيْرَاءُ: Humaira (a nickname for Aisha, meaning 'the red-faced one' or 'fair-skinned')

ai.seo_question: What did Aisha say to Imam Ali after the Battle of Jamal?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) addresses Aisha as 'Hamira' (the young camel), a term of endearment that underscores the familial bond between the Prophet’s household and his wives even amidst political conflict. Her response, 'You have won, so be generous' (or 'pardon generously'), is interpreted by scholars as a request for magnanimous treatment rather than mere political submission, highlighting the virtue of *'afw* (pardoning) in the Shia ethical tradition. This incident serves as a foundational example of how the Ahl al-Bayt prioritized grace and mercy over retribution in the aftermath of the Battle of Jamal.
